newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- OCT 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- OCT 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government is playing a risky game in allowing speculation over whether or not state titles and banking products will be the subject of new taxes in the 1997 budget to continue. Yesterday saw a forex outflow of approximately 500 million dollars but the Bank of Greece is unconcerned. --The government is to discuss the issue of wage increases for public servants at its meeting with unionists tomorrow and is expected to consider alternate scenarios.
--Teacher's unions threaten a 48-hour strike at the end of the month if a solution to understaffing problems is not found promptly.

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos tells Parliament about the appointment of publisher Stavros Psyharis as governor of the monastic community of Mount Athos. --Olympic Airways slashes prices by up to 58 percent . --Only urgent needs in the public sector - with priority to the sectors of health and education - will be covered next year, with seasonal employment cut back.

--Ignoring the complaints of smaller retailers and employees, 70 leading retailers get the go-ahead to extend trading hours to 8 p.m. on Saturday. The response from workers is a work stoppage beginning from 3 p.m.
--Furore in the Navy General Staff over use of the frigate 'Averoff' as the studio for a popular morning show. Navy General Staff chief submits his resignation.

--The situation in state schools explosive: 6,500 teaching positions vacant, school buildings lacking, strikes planned. Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis asks National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou for 18 billion drachmas to cover urgent needs. The answer: there are no funds. Teachers scale back on weekly teaching programme.
